summary.name: ShortcutCycle
summary.one_liner: A macOS app that groups apps by task and lets you switch within each group using a dedicated keyboard shortcut.
use_cases: Switch quickly between browsers or dev tools
Keep work and personal browser profiles separate
Jump to writing or chat apps with one shortcut
Automate app switching from Raycast, Alfred, or Shortcuts
Toggle a single app on and off with a hotkey
summary.what_it_does: ShortcutCycle lets you put apps into named groups, such as Browsers, Dev, or Social, and assign a keyboard shortcut to each group. Tapping the shortcut cycles through only the apps in that group, while holding it shows a preview of the selected app. Each group can be set to switch only among running apps or to launch the next closed app. It can also keep Chrome, Firefox, or Edge profiles distinct and exposes URL-scheme commands for automation tools such as Apple Shortcuts, Alfred, Raycast, and Keyboard Maestro. It switches apps rather than individual windows.
notable: Per-group shortcuts such as Option+1 always reach the same app group
Tap to switch, hold to preview the selected app
Automation via shortcutcycle:// URLs and Apple Shortcuts, Alfred, Raycast, Keyboard Maestro
Open source under MIT license, no analytics, automatic setup backups
caveats: Switches between apps, not individual windows
One-time price of $3.99 per the page (listing also marks it as freeware and open source)
